title: Near Future: IR + Infinitive
summary: Express plans and intentions with vou, vai, vamos, and vão plus an infinitive.

sections.heading: The structure
sections.body:
Brazilian Portuguese usually expresses the near future with **ir + infinitive**, much like 'going to' in English. Conjugate **ir** and leave the main verb in the infinitive.

| Subject | ir + infinitive |
|---|---|
| eu | vou estudar |
| você/ele/ela | vai estudar |
| nós | vamos estudar |
| vocês/eles/elas | vão estudar |

examples.en: I am going to travel tomorrow.
She is going to buy bread.
We are going to watch the game.

sections.heading: Plans, predictions, and intentions
sections.body: Use this structure for personal plans, expected events, and decisions made now. It is the most common future form in speech.

examples.en: It is going to rain tonight.
They are going to arrive early.

sections.heading: Negatives and questions
sections.body: Put **não** before the conjugated form of **ir**. Questions usually keep the same word order and use intonation.

examples.en: I am not going out today.
Are you going to work tomorrow?
Are we going to eat now?

keyPoints: Near future = ir in the present + infinitive.
It is the default future in everyday Brazilian speech.
Only ir is conjugated; the main verb stays in the infinitive.
A gente vai is very common for 'we are going to'.

commonMistakes.note: Do not add para in the future structure.
